data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"21 pencils cost $6, but only under the mechanism that the store honors the posted rate as a linear price function f(n) = (n/7) \u00d7 $2 for integer n divisible by 7, with no transaction frictions.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the store's pricing policy is not a linear function (e.g., has discontinuities, caps, or tiers), f(21) \u2260 $6.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the policy does not extend to n = 21 (e.g., max purchase is 7), the function is undefined at 21.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the posted rate is not the policy's actual function (e.g., bait-and-switch), the mechanism misrepresents the cause.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The mechanist mechanism requires an explicit causal link from the posted rate to the total cost. The posted rate defines a linear price function over pencils: f(n) = ($2/7) \u00d7 n. For n = 21, f(21) = ($2/7) \u00d7 21 = $6. The causal link is the store's pricing policy, which maps quantity to price via a constant unit rate.
